title: Views, copies and keys that change

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Code keeps safe = Collections.unmodifiableSet(original) and later calls original.add("c"). What does safe.contains("c") give?

options.text: false, because the returned set copied the elements when it was made.
options.says: Copying is what Set.copyOf does; unmodifiableSet wraps the original set without copying it.

options.text: true, because the returned set reads its elements from original.
options.says: unmodifiableSet returns a read-only view, so later changes to the original show through it.

options.text: an UnsupportedOperationException, because original was changed afterwards.
options.says: The view refuses changes made through it; changes made to the original are allowed and reading the view still works.

questions.stem: A HashMap's key is an ArrayList. After put(key, "value"), the code calls key.add("b") and then map.get(key). What happens?

options.text: It returns "value", since the same list object is passed back to get.
options.says: HashMap locates the entry by the key's current hash first; the list's hash changed with its contents, so the lookup goes astray.

options.text: It throws ConcurrentModificationException, since the key changed inside the map.
options.says: HashMap does not track changes to its keys; the lookup simply fails to find the entry.

options.text: It returns null, since the list's new hash code leads to a different bucket.
options.says: Adding an element changes the list's hashCode, so get searches where the entry is not and the entry becomes unreachable.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: Changing a HashMap key after it was put changes its hash, so the entry can no longer be found.
Collections.unmodifiableSet is a read-only view that shows later changes to the original, while Set.copyOf and Set.of are immutable copies.
